sources.title: Wikipedia GeoSearch, 2.5 km radius around downtown Dallas
National Register of Historic Places listings in Dallas County, Texas

stops.name: Dealey Plaza
stops.description: The triangular park where Elm, Main and Commerce converge, laid out in the 1930s on the site of Dallas's first settlement and known worldwide for one minute in 1963.

stops.name: Texas School Book Depository
stops.description: The 1901 warehouse whose sixth-floor corner window made it the most examined building in America; it houses the county offices and the Sixth Floor Museum today.

stops.name: John Fitzgerald Kennedy Memorial
stops.description: Philip Johnson's roofless concrete box, a cenotaph designed to be walked into and stood inside rather than looked at from outside.

stops.name: Dallas County Courthouse
stops.description: The 1892 red sandstone and granite courthouse locals call Old Red, saved from demolition and now a county history museum.

stops.name: Pioneer Park Cemetery
stops.description: Four merged nineteenth-century burial grounds holding many of the city's founders, marooned between the convention center and the freeway.

stops.name: Pioneer Plaza
stops.description: Seventy bronze longhorns driven by three trail riders across a landscaped slope, one of the largest such sculpture groups anywhere.

stops.name: Dallas Union Station
stops.description: The 1916 beaux-arts terminal that once consolidated five railroads' passenger traffic and still serves Amtrak, DART and the TRE.

stops.name: Reunion Tower
stops.description: The 1978 geodesic sphere on a concrete stalk whose lights are the one piece of the skyline everyone can name.

stops.name: Dallas Municipal Building
stops.description: The 1914 city hall and police headquarters where Jack Ruby shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the basement garage.

stops.name: Majestic Theatre
stops.description: The last survivor of Elm Street's Theatre Row, a 1921 vaudeville and film palace now the city's oldest working theatre.

stops.name: Wilson Building
stops.description: A 1904 beaux-arts department store block modelled on Paris's Grand Hotel du Louvre, converted to apartments.

stops.name: Kirby Building
stops.description: Adolphus Busch's 1913 gothic revival tower, built as the Busch Building and among the first Dallas skyscrapers turned residential.

stops.name: Magnolia Hotel
stops.description: The 1922 oil-company headquarters carrying the red neon Pegasus, the flying horse that has served as the city's unofficial emblem since 1934.

stops.name: Adolphus Hotel
stops.description: The 1912 baroque hotel a St. Louis brewer built because he thought Dallas deserved better, still the grandest room downtown.

stops.name: Thanks-Giving Square
stops.description: A wedge of park sunk below street level around Philip Johnson's spiral chapel, whose stained-glass ceiling turns as you look up.

note: Every stop has an English Wikipedia article carrying coordinates. Street addresses are taken from the NRHP Dallas County listing rows or from the article's own infobox; where neither gives one the address is left null rather than derived from coordinates. ZIP is left null throughout - no source consulted in this run states it, and the importer backfills blanks without overwriting a human.
